entry.title: Heavy Snow Watch
entry.summary: Periods of heavy snow above 800 metres, where snowfall amounts may approach warning criteria. Note, lesser amounts of snow could fall as low as 400 metres. Chance of upgrading to a Warning: Moderate. Changes: The validity of this Watch has been shortened and it now ends 6pm Thursday.

author.name: Meteorological Service of New Zealand Limited

entry.title: Heavy Rain Warning - Orange
entry.summary: Expect 70 to 90 mm of rain, especially about the Paparoa Range. Peak rates of 10 to 20 mm/h. Impact: Streams and rivers may rise rapidly. Surface flooding, slips, and difficult driving conditions possible. Chance of upgrading to a Red Warning: Minimal. Changes: Watch upgraded to an Orange Warning.

author.name: Meteorological Service of New Zealand Limited

entry.title: Heavy Rain Warning - Orange
entry.summary: Expect 300 to 450 mm of rain about the ranges, and 150 to 200 mm nearer the coast. Peak rates of 20 to 30 mm/h expected this afternoon and evening, then again from Thursday afternoon to Friday morning about the ranges. Impact: Streams and rivers may rise rapidly. Surface flooding, slips, and difficult driving conditions possible. Chance of upgrading to a Red Warning: Low.

entry.title: Heavy Rain Watch
entry.summary: Periods of heavy rain. Rainfall amounts may approach warning criteria within 20 km east of the main divide. Note, rain is expected turn to snow this evening. Another burst of heavy rain is expected Thursday evening to Friday morning and a new Watch or Warning may be issued closer to the time. Chance of upgrading to a Warning: Low.

entry.summary: Snow lowering to 400-500 metres in the morning. Expect 10-15 cm to accumulate over the summit with a LOW risk of around 25cm, mainly falling in the morning. Lesser amounts to lower levels.

entry.title: Road Snowfall Warning
entry.summary: Brief snowfall is possible about the road until 4pm Wednesday afternoon but little, if any, is expected to settle on the road near the summit. A period of heavier snow is expected Thursday morning and afternoon. Between 5am and 3pm Thursday, 2 to 5 cm could settle on the road near the summit (possibly as much 10 cm) with lesser amounts to 500 metres.
